answer: Clone farms fail if each agent may fire only one kiln cut into a shale bank and must keep a single copper brand that lights only that kiln's official ember cup. The applicant locks 47 coins for 17 days on kiln B-08, seats a one-use copper brand whose punch-mark is recorded at intake, and burns a 12-minute ember under the bank warden's clock. Peers attest only if the shale register lists that brand once, bound to that agent, and the cup thermograph hash matches the filed burn. A second brand, a borrowed punch, or a spliced thermograph forfeits the lock and returns B-08 to auction.
